newsitem.title: USA: Halliburton unit wins U.S. Army contract.
newsitem.headline: Halliburton unit wins U.S. Army contract.

text.p: Halliburton Co said Monday its Brown & Root Government Services unit has won a one-year U.S. Army contract worth at least $137.9 million to continue providing logistics support to American forces in the Balkans.
The company said the contract runs through May 1998 and has two, six-month options that could bring the total value to $270 million.

The contract calls for Brown & Root to provide such services as base camp maitenance, basic life support, food, water, laundry, equipment maintenance and transportation for the 8,500 U.S. peace-keeping troops stationed in the Balkans, the company said.

Brown & Roots had provided the same services to American forces in the Balkans since November 1995 under the Army's Logistics Civil Augmentation Program (LOGCAP), it said. While the new sustainment contract calls for the same services to be provided, it is not part of the LOGCAP program.
